  - `driverCompilesReadableIdsLeaf` is `supports.readableIdsLeaf === true` exactly; the `SEMI_JOIN_COMPILING_DRIVERS` name set is gone (not re-exported by any package index on `main`), and `relationSemiJoinServes` reads the bit. The engine binds `relationReadDriver` to its own `getDriver`.

The analytics bridge passes `refusal` through, and `executeCrossObjectJoined` throws it before the `joined: false` → FK-expand fallback.

The dimension pins assert `{ code: 'INVALID_QUERY', status: 400 }` on the outcome (engine) and on the thrown error (service, real `SqliteWasmDriver` re-declared without the bit, zero driver reads, no FK-expand).
- **Controls and ablations:** a driver named MongoDB that declares the bit plans the semi-join (the bit, not the name); Turso / memory shape with the bit is declined and served by the FK-expand with the reference rows. Ablations in os-dev-report 6935291273: A (where throw removed) → 1 red, B (aggregate refusal disabled) → 3 + 1 red, C (`throw answer.refusal` removed) → 1 red, each restored to the HEAD blob.
- **Forced test changes:** `credential-evaluation-guard`, `query-expression-conformance` and `engine-readable-ids-nested-composition` doubles now declare the bit; their assertions are unchanged (the body names each).
- **Consumer layer:** a grep of `content/`, `skills/`, `packages/**/src` and the ADRs at this head for "compiles no subquery" / "keeps the id read" finds no sentence left that sends MongoDB/OData to the id read on a read verb. Two skill files still teach the capped id read on every driver: `skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md:373` and `rules/filters.md:96`. That is what `Skills-docs: follow-up #33875` points at; see "Before landing".
- **Dogfood battery (narrowing):** on this head under the verify lock, 478 files passed / 3 skipped, 4054 tests passed / 68 skipped, VERDICT command-exit 0 (final-head comment 6937664173, `objectstack-seat2/33876-dogfood-reading.txt`). Derived gates 125/125.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc31d3f7b6c50ed7c720d61bbea6f9f5c9840b29`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-query-lowering.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-semi-join.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-group-join.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/types.ts; narrowing floor: every other non-prose path of the diff (packages/spec/src/data/driver.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, the eight test files under packages/objectql, packages/drivers and packages/services/service-analytics); read to judge, not reviewed: packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/read-scope-sql.ts, docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md, AGENTS.md

### ① Derived judgments

- Inputs read: card #33876 body and its three comments; PR #34565 body, file list (28 files) and net diff against its merge base with `main`; the 72 check-runs on this head (60 success, 12 skipped, none red, none pending); the cited rulings 6889543194 and 6889549817 on #33626 and the seat route on #33664.
- `DriverCapabilitiesSchema` gains `readableIdsLeaf: z.boolean().optional()`. Accept set widened by one optional key; a non-boolean is refused; absence parses to no key. Right. The `DriverCapabilities` type gains one optional member; every in-repo `supports` literal still type-checks (TypeScript Type Check green).
- Live-bit count: 7 at this head (`queryDateGranularity`, `autonumber`, `batchSchemaSync`, `transactionsUnsupported`, `aggregationFilter`, `lockRows`, `readableIdsLeaf`) plus 31 tombstones. Right for `main` as it stands: `main` carries 6 (with `lockRows`), and `zonedDateBucketing` (#34530) is not on it.
- Who declares the bit, read on every driver's `supports`: `SqlDriver` (getter, every dialect), `SqliteWasmDriver` (inherits, no override), `TursoDriver` (spreads `super.supports`; its remote path resolves the leaf through `remoteReadableIdsSemiJoin`), `InMemoryDriver` (evaluates the leaf in process, ruling 6889549817). `MongoDBDriver` (`batchSchemaSync`, `queryDateGranularity`) and `ODataDriver` (`transactionsUnsupported`) do not, and both refuse the leaf in their own filter path. The declaring set equals the removed `SEMI_JOIN_COMPILING_DRIVERS` name set member for member, so no in-repo driver changes side. Right.
- `SEMI_JOIN_COMPILING_DRIVERS` is removed. It was an `export const` of a module the package index does not re-export (`index.ts` exports only `RELATION_FILTER_ID_CAP` from this family), and nothing outside `packages/objectql/src` named it. No public removal. Right.
- The narrowing, where half. Accepted before, refused now, on a driver whose `supports.readableIdsLeaf` is not exactly `true` (MongoDB, OData, any third-party driver that does not declare it): a `where` holding a condition beneath a single-valued relation field (`{ account: { region: 'NA' } }`, at any depth of `$and` / `$or` / `$not`) on `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate`. Before: the related ids were read as the caller and the read was served up to 1,000 related matches (past 1,000 it was already `INVALID_FILTER` / 400). Now: `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 before any read, on every such query. Stated by the body and the changeset. Right as a statement.
- The same narrowing reaches two analytics shapes the body does not name: an analytics `where` leaf through a lookup, and a dataset's own `filter` through a lookup, both of which `ObjectQLStrategy` hands the engine as that nested-relation condition (`servedWhere`, `servedScope`). On those drivers they are refused by the same engine door. See N4.
- The narrowing, dimension half. Accepted before, refused now, on the same drivers: an analytics query with a dimension through a lookup (`opportunity.stage` on a line cube) when the host bridges the engine (`executeRelationGroupAggregate` wired, the plugin's default). Before: declined by the engine and served by the FK-expand. Now: `INVALID_QUERY` / 400, nothing read. A host that wires its own `executeAggregate` never asks the engine and keeps the FK-expand. Stated by the body. Right as a statement.
- Unchanged, checked in the code: a multi-valued relation condition and the `where` of `update` / `delete` keep the capped id read on every driver; the fallbacks `relationSemiJoinServes` names (a hook or object middleware on the related object, another datasource, a federated related object, a tenancy-class mismatch under a walled posture) keep the id read on a declaring driver.
- The widening: the leaf is planned for any driver that declares the bit, whatever its name. A third-party driver that declares it takes on ADR-0139 D3's compile obligation, tenant wall included. Right, and the TSDoc says who should not declare it.
- `RelationGroupOutcome` gains `{ kind: 'refused', error }` and `RelationGroupAggregateAnswer` gains an optional `refusal` on its `joined: false` arm. Both additive; a host-supplied hook that never sets `refusal` behaves as before. Right.
- Error codes: `INVALID_FILTER` and `INVALID_QUERY` are both members of the standard catalog (`StandardErrorCode`, `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`) and both appear on the ledger page. Neither is a new code, so no ledger row is owed, and the lint and repo-gate check-runs, which carry the error-code gates, are green on this head. The dimension refusal stamps `StandardErrorCode.enum.INVALID_QUERY`, status and `httpStatus` 400, `param: 'groupBy'`. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: `yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and on the changeset, the same line in both. Right: the diff widens (a new optional spec key; the leaf by bit, not by name) and narrows (the two refusals above).

`Metadata-protocol: added` with `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`; `objectql`, `driver-sql`, `driver-memory` and `service-analytics` at `patch`. This matches AGENTS.md: the kind `added` takes at least `minor` on the package that gains the key, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner. The changeset carries the banner, the FROM and TO mapping, both declaration lines and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which is the right disposition: nothing stored is rewritten. `driver-mongodb` gains a test only and publishes nothing new. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (route to contract review): answered by this record.
- open_questions 2 (Clause-② arm): `yes (narrowing)` is right. The premise re-measurement is correct against `main`: a driver outside the name set got the capped id read, not a 500.
- open_questions 3 (dimension code): `INVALID_QUERY` is right. It is the standard code the aggregate door already uses for a group-key refusal, a dimension is not a filter, and the scope note asks for the same stable 400, which it is.
- open_questions 4 (the bit's name): `readableIdsLeaf` names the leaf ADR-0139 defines and is acceptable. It is a published key, so the Tier H approver confirms the name when landing.
- open_questions 5 (landing order against ADR-0139): escalated to the Tier H approver. Ruling 6889543194 says the PR carries an ADR-0139 amendment, and the card lists the amendment as item 1 of what lands. This head carries none, and ADR-0139 D3 on `main` still reads that no `DriverCapabilities` bit returns. The amendment is a governed surface outside this card's file surface, so it is not a finding on this diff, but the approver should land this PR with the amendment card filed and linked, not after an open-ended gap.
- Authority for the dimension half: ruling A (6889543194) names a cross-object `where` only. The dimension refusal rests on scope note 6917475155, the epic rule quoted on #33664 (MongoDB and OData refuse with a stable 400) and Prime Directive 5 (ruling record 6888468549). The seat route on #33664 says in its own words that it is not a maintainer ruling. Sufficient to judge the design; the approver should know which authority it lands on.
- Deviations: `Metadata-protocol: added` in place of the claim's `none` is forced by the authorable-surface shard and is right. The two docs pages and the regenerated driver pages are prose and generated output, not reviewed. The MongoDB pin is a sound guard against the bit being declared while the filter translation refuses the leaf.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no new in-app join. The change removes an id-read path on drivers without the bit and replaces it with a refusal, which is what Prime Directive 5 asks for. On a declaring SQL driver the single-valued read-verb condition stays one nested subquery. The id reads that remain (multi-valued relation, write verbs, the named fallbacks) and the FK-expand on `driver-memory` and Turso all predate this PR and are unchanged by it.
- Refusal order: the where refusal runs at `where` admission, before the middleware chain and before the related object's own doors; the dimension refusal runs before the aggregate doors. No scope, tenant-wall or permission filter is dropped or reordered on a served path: the refused paths serve nothing, and the served paths are the code `main` runs. A caller with no access to the related object reads a 400 in place of a 403; the message names only what the caller wrote, plus the driver name the ruling asks for.
- Cross-repo note: a driver outside this repository that builds its own `supports` literal instead of spreading `SqlDriver`'s loses the nested-relation condition until it declares the bit. The changeset says so for third-party drivers.
- Landing note (collision with #34530): this head is right for `main` today. #34530 also adds a live bit and moves the same pin and the generated driver pages to seven. Whichever lands second merges `main`, moves the pin in `packages/spec/src/data/driver.test.ts` to eight (both the roster and the two count strings), and regenerates the driver reference pages. The PR body already plans to land second.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`, against rulings 6889543194 and 6889549817 and its first consumer. The bit holds. Method presence cannot carry the signal (every driver has `find()`), which is the file's own rule for a live bit. The reader lands in the same change (`driverCompilesReadableIdsLeaf`, three call sites, `=== true` exactly, so a truthy string does not pass). The `.describe()` text and the header roster agree with the code. I tried to break it through an inheriting driver that cannot honour the bit (Turso remote: it compiles the leaf with its own transport), through a wrapper driver with its own `supports` (none in the tree), through a read verb that skips the door (`find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate` are the only four operations that reach it, all pinned), and through a mixed `where` (the first single-valued site refuses the whole read before any id read, pinned under `$or` and `$not`).
